body.name: Mars
body.atmosphere: Thin CO2-dominated atmosphere with dust, water-ice clouds, and strong seasonal effects.
body.surface: Basaltic crust, iron-oxide dust, volcanic provinces, canyon systems, impact basins, polar layered deposits, and ancient water-modified terrain.

textures.surfaceCredit: Solar System Scope / Wikimedia Commons Mars texture map
textures.heightmapCredit: NASA PDS Mars Global Surveyor MOLA MEGDR median topography
textures.heightmapResolution: 5760 x 2880 samples at 16 pixels per degree, resampled to a 2048 x 1024 WebGL displacement map
textures.textureNote: Surface color is a public global texture; 3D terrain and relief shading are derived from NASA PDS MOLA topography and vertically exaggerated for readability.

sources.label: NASA Mars facts
sources.note: Planetary constants, day length, gravity, orbit, and moon context.

sources.label: NASA Mars Trek
sources.note: Reference portal for Mars surface mapping, contextual layers, and mission geography.

sources.label: NASA PDS MOLA MEGDR
sources.note: Mars Global Surveyor laser-altimeter topography used for the WebGL terrain displacement and hillshade.

features.name: Olympus Mons
features.scale: about 600 km wide; summit about 21.9 km above Mars datum
features.summary: Largest known volcano in the Solar System, located on the Tharsis rise.
features.source: IAU/USGS nomenclature and NASA Mars reference mapping

features.name: Valles Marineris
features.scale: more than 4,000 km long and up to about 7 km deep
features.summary: A vast equatorial canyon system that exposes tectonic and erosional history.
features.source: NASA Mars Trek / IAU feature reference

features.name: Hellas Planitia
features.scale: about 2,300 km wide; one of the deepest basins on Mars
features.summary: Ancient southern-hemisphere impact basin with a strong topographic signature.
features.source: NASA Mars reference mapping / USGS feature nomenclature

features.name: Argyre Planitia
features.summary: Large southern highland basin surrounded by rugged ancient terrain.
features.source: NASA Mars Trek / USGS feature nomenclature

features.name: Gale Crater
features.summary: Curiosity rover landing region; layered Mount Sharp records long environmental change.
features.source: NASA Mars Science Laboratory landing-site reference

features.name: Jezero Crater
features.summary: Perseverance rover landing region containing an ancient river-delta system.

features.name: Utopia Planitia
features.summary: Northern plains region visited by Viking 2 and Zhurong.

features.name: Isidis Planitia
features.summary: Large basin east of Syrtis Major, near the Jezero landing region.

features.name: Syrtis Major Planum
features.summary: A classic telescopic albedo feature and ancient volcanic plateau.

features.name: Nili Fossae
features.summary: Carbonate- and clay-bearing terrain important for ancient-water studies.
features.source: NASA Mars mineralogy context / USGS nomenclature

features.name: Elysium Mons
features.scale: about 240 km wide; about 13 km high
features.summary: Major shield volcano in the Elysium volcanic province.

features.name: Tharsis Montes
features.scale: three giant shield volcanoes spanning the Tharsis region
features.summary: Arsia, Pavonis, and Ascraeus Montes form a major volcanic alignment.
features.source: NASA Mars Trek / USGS feature reference

features.name: Noctis Labyrinthus
features.scale: maze-like trough system west of Valles Marineris
features.summary: Complex collapsed and faulted terrain marking the transition from Tharsis to Valles Marineris.

features.name: Korolev Crater
features.summary: Northern crater famous for a persistent water-ice deposit.
features.source: ESA/NASA Mars surface reference and USGS feature coordinates

features.name: Planum Boreum
features.summary: Layered water-ice and dust deposits recording climate cycles.

features.name: Planum Australe
features.summary: Southern polar layered deposits and seasonal CO2 frost region.

landingSites.name: Viking 1
landingSites.summary: First successful U.S. Mars lander in Chryse Planitia.

landingSites.name: Viking 2
landingSites.summary: Utopia Planitia lander that operated through 1980.

landingSites.name: Mars Pathfinder / Sojourner
landingSites.summary: Demonstrated low-cost landing and rover operations in Ares Vallis.

landingSites.name: Spirit
landingSites.summary: MER rover that explored Gusev Crater and Columbia Hills.

landingSites.name: Opportunity
landingSites.summary: MER rover that crossed Meridiani Planum and Endeavour Crater.

landingSites.name: Phoenix
landingSites.summary: Polar lander that sampled near-surface water ice.

landingSites.name: Curiosity
landingSites.summary: Mars Science Laboratory rover studying Gale Crater and Mount Sharp.

landingSites.name: InSight
landingSites.summary: Geophysical lander that measured marsquakes and interior structure.

landingSites.name: Perseverance
landingSites.summary: Mars 2020 rover caching samples and studying Jezero Crater.

landingSites.name: Zhurong
landingSites.summary: Tianwen-1 rover landing site in southern Utopia Planitia.

moons.name: Phobos
moons.summary: Inner, larger moon orbiting faster than a Martian day.

moons.name: Deimos
moons.summary: Outer, smaller moon with a slower, more distant orbit.

notes.coordinates: Feature coordinates are approximate center points in planetographic/IAU-style Mars reference context, normalized to -180 to +180 longitude for the AstroBis map.
notes.visualization: This is a real-data WebGL atlas, not a rover-scale GIS terrain engine. The surface color, MOLA displacement, MOLA hillshade, markers, polar haze, and labels are separate layers.
